I'm only really commenting because Steam forces me to when leaving a review. Keep in mind this isn't a bash, I actually see this game having a lot of promise.

While the movement is indeed fluid and fun, and the visuals are stunning, it still lacks a lot of quality of life features to make it worth coming back to.
For example: what is each enemy? All I see is their shots following me; the only one that stood out to me so far is the Mammoth, because of how distinct -- and annoying -- it is, with its large damage and being extremely tanky.

Why is the hub portal a consumable item instead of just having the pause menu allow us to quit to the hub? Why isn't there a button to see the objectives again instead of having us commit it to memory?

Is it normal to always be dying randomly because there is nothing like at least an indicator as to where shots and enemies are coming from? Everything being glowing means it's very hard to discern between enemies and props unless you look at them against the floor or against a wall.

Why are the resources so hard to come by in a mobility shooter? Having a nimble but frail character does nothing if I can't actually shoot back at the things I'm escaping from. More than once was I forced to retreat back to the usual 'shoot from cover' kind of gameplay one sees in other FPS games just because leaving it meant I would die immediately to the unrelenting horde that does not return enough health or take enough damage from melee to justify running through.

My biggest problem is the tutorial; it only really teaches you how to control your character. All other things are meant to be figured out normally -- which is not a problem for me, honestly -- but everything happens so all at once there is barely any time to look at items, enemies and resources as separate things instead of clumping them all in one box of "shoot everything and mash interact".

GTTOD has many merits and understands its references well, and I can see how it can become a great game in the future, but right now it falls short in understanding how to tie all of those together in an enjoyable way. Especially about progression; the game has so many weapons and I barely get to see any of them because the enemies get stronger each run, and the player doesn't unless they manage to farm enough shards or get lucky with a crate. It tries to do too many things at once, to its detriment.

I fought against the decision of asking for a refund, and now I continue to play the game to accompany its development and see for myself how far it has come from the skeletal stage it is in at the time of writing.

This is an update on my review of GTTOD. My review was previously a negative one, and unfortunately, it's going to stay this way even after playing the update. I will also be talking about the developer's response to my negative review of the previous update.

I've been playing GTTOD since 2019, and I really, really had high hopes for the game. GTTOD used to be an endless shooter in a neon synthwave environment, and I believed that all the game needed was more content, because the gameplay and aesthetics were spot on. However, the developer decided that he hated the game, and wanted to completely rework the whole thing, and turn it into a completely different game. The biggest change is switching from a doom-style endless shooter to some Risk of Rain Roguelike FPS game. This new update is around the 3rd or 4th complete overhaul for GTTOD, where he completely changed the mechanics and alienating a lot of his older playerbase in the process.

Before getting into my issues with the game, I want to talk about the good things first. The movement is much better than it was before, in fact, it is the only thing keeping me from uninstalling the game. The animations are decent and the game looks better graphically than it did in previous updates. The new music is also good.

Now, for the stuff I personally dislike, I think with every update to this game, it loses more and more of what I enjoyed about the game in the previous version. Again, I'm not telling the developer what he can and cannot do, I'm just speaking from my own personal feelings towards the game.

In the previous update, the one thing that was keeping me entertained with this game is the Endless Mode, and although I complained about the Crevice map being completely broken and the game forcing me to play through some horribly designed parkour sequence every time I wanted to play a round of Endless Mode, it was still fun to be able to kill hordes of enemies, parkouring in a small arena, while grinding money to upgrade guns. For me, it was the closest the game's ever been since in rekindling what I really enjoyed about the old 2019 version.

With this new update, instead of improving Endless Mode and fixing the unplayable level, he decided to just completely remove Endless Mode entirely. In fact, now there's only one game mode in the game. Players who wanted something closer to the 2019 version would now have no choice but to play the main roguelike mode, which I also have some problems with.

The game tries really hard to be a roguelike, which is fine, but I think it is poorly executed. The game doesn't know what it wants to be. The movement is super fast, and the compass points RIGHT TOWARDS the exit door, which seems to encourage players to just disregard everything and run right towards the exit (and for the first few levels, there is no consequence for ignoring everything). This makes every level super fast to beat. The is no real incentive to doing anything else, the game barely teaches you what the mechanics are, you are just left to figure things out for yourself, which contradicts how the game encourages you to just ignore everything and get to the exit as fast as possible.

In previous versions, there is a really obvious screen effect for when you are at low health, which tells you CLEARLY that you are about to die. However, with this update, all you get is a beeping sound effect with no other clear indications on screen other than your health bar, and since enemies can kill you super quickly, it can lead to unfair deaths where you didn't notice that you're at low health, and enemies just killing you in a few seconds. 

To add insult to injury, every time you die, you have to sit through a really long death animation, which is unskippable. You will then be teleported to some weird area where you can upgrade yourself, but most of the time, you won't have enough currency to upgrade anything, but the game still forces you to sit through it. Once you're done with that, you'll have to watch ANOTHER long and unskippable cutscene of the player getting up and wiping water off his helmet before the game will let you play again. This is really irritating because of how frequent you may die, and how long it takes for you to get back into the action. This wouldn't be so bad if the animations are skippable, but they're not. Imagine if ULTRAKILL forced you to watch 30 seconds of animations before letting you respawn...

The developer of this game responded to my negative review in the past, where he reassured me that he's working on addressing the issues I had with the game, and told me that the mechanics he's working on will allow those who didn't like the roguelike direction GTTOD is going towards to enjoy the game more. He mentioned something called "The Cinder Core", which he said was a level that is comprised of mini arenas. This level is nowhere to be found, maybe it's in the update under a different name, but I cannot find it. I did find some portal that will lead to a dungeon, but you'll need shards or something to unlock it, and the game doesn't tell you what those dungeons are. Andrew also talked about adding a Prologue which will better explain the mechanics, this is also not present in the update, and if it is, it sure does a terrible job at teaching players anything. Andrew also talked about adding Quick Play, which is also something completely not present in this update. 

Basically, none of the things the developer said he would be adding in his response to my review are actually here. Instead of trying to add features to the game that players who liked the old versions would enjoy and polishing up what he made in the past, he removed and remade more and more things that further alienates those players. I am noticing a trend here.

I really enjoyed GTTOD back in the day, and I believed that it has a lot of potential. But all these unnecessary overhauls just really put a sour taste in my mouth, further drifting away from what made the old versions so fun to play. I am willing to bet that Andrew is going to completely overhaul everything again in a few months. 

Andrew constantly made the game more and more convoluted, complicating things and removing what made the old versions so much fun. I know I'm in the minority, and I am aware that a lot of people enjoy how GTTOD became a roguelike game, and good for them. But I personally don't see the game being what I originally hoped it was going to be anymore. It looks like it's time to let go.

GTTOD is fun, it has it's own visual style that should age well and it has decent gameplay loop but.. for 20 bucks there isn't much. Before I rant a bit, I'll just say game good but there's a lot of fixable gripes right now. 

So now for bullet list of those gripes.

There's only a handful of levels and this is apparently the update before 1.0, even if he did add another "act" of levels, the game would be incredibly short and still not worth 20 bucks.

There's only 2 real bosses and they're both melee focused with some ranged attacks, in a game where you're effectively a ninja monkey on 12 experimental enhancer drugs and that's without the upgrades. Yeah dev didn't think boss design that well.

Movement feels great as if you can speed and soar into the air, but the design of the levels seems to want to keep me to the ground. Yeah there are wall run spots everywhere but nothing screams verticality, anything that has a whimper of it fails to keep it consistent and the enemy ai..

The AI is simplistic completely. They just walk at you and do X attack. Some (IMP) try to do a unique position spot so they can spam ranged at you but a majority just walk at you even when they're range based. 

In addition the maps have MANY zones where the player can just be safe, regen shields and even throw grenades/c4 down at the enemy to wipe them. If the player wants to cheese the game it's incredibly easy to, even the bosses aren't immune to this.

The challenge area, abyss or whatever, is completely pointless beyond farming. There is no way to escape it that at least I could find, it's endless dropping that is completely disconnected from the main game's setup so.. why does it exist? It's not actually challenging, you're just dropped into a arena and kill a bunch of guys to get a reward. Since you can't return there's no reason to go into it on a normal run, its purely just to farm and for a rogue game that's... bad imo. The main game should facilitate said farm, not some side area. If anything it just further tells me that this Rogue-like aspect of it was tacked on.

There are many small tiny issues concerning sound design and animation, for instance many inspect animations do not have sounds yet and/or are very VERY basic animations while others have a full visual flare to them. Also inspect animation sounds and camera movement does not stop if you swap off weapon, funny.

The dev, for whatever insane reason that just contributes to the idea that he's just cobbling together ideas, added a fishing minigame. No wonder this game's taking so long to finish.

The game lets you acquire "card packs" from the get go at random, these are supposed to give cards that will, for one time, change your starting equipment. This mechanic is fine and I like the idea. What I don't like is the only way to access this is to level up your character about 3? 4? whole bars in the upgrade tree, which takes awhile since you dont have the challenge area to farm as it's also locked, just to get the guy who lets you use these cards to open. This "shop" should be open either from the get go or when the player finishes the first level up bar of the upgrade system. Not several.

I want to say I like this game, but all these minor gripes add up and the fact that they're touting a 20 dollar front and from what I can tell it was previously 15 bucks for even less content? Is horrible. This game is $10 MAX at current state and unless their fabled 1.0 update adds another 2-3 acts, it should never be above $15 after release.

And the funny thing is, I didn't even pay for it, my friend got me it as a gift, I still feel like it was overpriced. When 1.0 drops I'll check it out and redo the review, for now this is what I have to say : Get it on discount, and I mean a GOOD discount. UNLESS 

IMPORTANT Edit : As one small thing, despite my gripes with the CURRENT pricetag for the CURRENT content. The dev could use the money, if you feel the game deserves the money regardless, fuckit pay full price. After actually checking their discord and talking with the dev myself they seem like they actually do want to keep making the game better and better and I hope they can achieve that.

Let me say that the game is filled to brim with potential. It has many redeeming qualities but is in no way polished or refined in the state its in. Far too many insecurities and things i dislike. It has the best movement i've ever seen in a game before. I get this rush of dopamine every damn time I land onto a wall and go straight for the WALLRUN. oh GOD THE WALLRUN. The force of gravity feels natural and flowy, and the speed acceleration is so extremely satisfying. The shooting is also alot of fun, its alot of fun to land those hits and land melee attacks like kicks and punches. You can even stomp the enemies!

Here's where things kinda suck.

THE GAMEPLAY: I love the platforming, the wallrunning, and many parts of the levels that are based on movement. But GOD its so extremely repetitive. Each level is an abnoxious arena survival where the enemies run at mach zero and will *never* catch up.. Like.. EVER. The level design is abhorrent and basically insults the speed and mobility that you are given. All these small platforms and skinny bridges give you the middle finger due to how much they dont work with your speed and the pacing of the game. Alongside the enemies which are absolute PUSHOVERS. Literally just feels like a point-and-click game. I've never seem myself on the edge of my seat while fighting. Reaching the extremely late waves which claim to be difficult, finding it to be nothing more but a race to see whether you can shoot before they start firing at you. PLEASE, IM BEGGING YOU TO INCREASE THE SPEED OF THE ENEMIES! Primarily what this game needs is a better environment, the enemies are slow and sluggish and it always feels like your speed is useless. You have NO reason to go full-speed and run across the map like you're able to because an opponent will NEVER bring you to do that. Enemies are too slow to chase you down and overwhelm you. Their bullets are too slow to feel like an actual threat, just something to encourage you to step to the left just a LITTLE. The stages are very claustrophobic and have a seemingly pointless high-ground where enemies barely move and take up space. You can avoid danger by just walking away, it'll take forever for them to do anything about it. We need a FASTER environment that can KEEP UP WITH US. This will make tensions higher and encourage us to use our insane mobility throughout the levels. I cannot stress how annoying it is to be able to run at mach 80 while these guys literally cannot move at ALL. Game would benefit from homing projectiles, chasing enemies, and literally anything that gets us to move. We should be outsmarting the enemies with our movement, not running away from them! Another thing is the guns, they all feel like they serve the same purpose. Automatic gun that shreds down hordes. Crowd control. Splash damage explosive weapon which is best for: crowd control. semi automatic weapons better at dealing individual damage but are mostly just: crowd control. The best we get are the single-fire weapons, these actually encourage us to aim and fire carefully and pick targets.

- THE GRAPHICS: dont get me wrong i love the neon aesthetic. Many of the sights and locations can be absolutely stunning but i hate the over-usage of neon outlines. All that depth that existed in the graphics are immediately destroyed due to the atrocious colors and the outlines which make everything blend together and look flat as all hell. More often than not it feels like style over substance. The use of bloom hurts my eyes, the pickups, props, and ESPECIALLY the enemies feel impossible to read because of all the effects and colors. The silhouettes of the enemies are even abstracted by the abnoxious glow effect. The only way to see which enemy is which is by their name, which you can see by hovering over them with your crosshair. This doesnt help because that'll become impossible to read through all the bullets and effects covering that, too. And besides, it only flashes for a second.

-EVERYTHING ELSE: Overall the game doesn't have much going for it aside from *some* fun gamemodes. But thats it. These gamemodes include new abilites, new guns, difficulty changes and an endless gamemode. These are fun but barely do anything to make up for what i had mentioned. Alot of my gripes in this game are based on fundamental features like the combat and gunplay. I do enjoy many of the tracks, but they're quite forgettable. The aesthetic and atmosphere of the game can extremely serene and relaxing here and there. But that's it.

Overall I dont think the game is worth it in the state its in. Thankfully its early access so its nowhere near its final state. But i definitely do wish it gets some sort of overhaul gameplay-wise. GTTOD feels like a casual experience just shooting enemies in the background until the next wave starts. The gameplay needs far more depth than what it is right now and feels very lacking. With a currency and shop systems that feel useless and unneeded. This game's design priorities feel like they're in the wrong place. They're far too focused on extra gamemodes, maps, new guns, instead of the base game itself. The pieces just wont come together. We need more attention on the level designs, the guns, and the combat especially.

I've followed this game for a few years now and it just got worse since I bought into early access.

First of all, the game requires you to kill enemies in quick succession to finish a level, but it doesn't spawn enough of them to do that for SO LONG on the first level that I get tired of it at that point already.

Second, it's supposed to be inspired by Titanfall 2, but in that game you don't get PUNISHED FOR MOVING. Here, enemies perfectly predict where you're going to be if you don't change direction, so instead of parkour, the best strategy is just spamming A,D and jump while staying in the same spot. You can't outrun their aim because it's predictive and you can't outrun bullets because they're very fast.

The enemies have gotten less distinguishable and less fun to fight. The game had an issue where they'd be to easy to fight or skip, but now one is annoying and the other is impossible.

The random level generation isn't what I'd consider good either. It just places platforms around - you're never locked into rooms that would force you to play a certain way, there's no variety, pickups aren't distributed in a way that makes sense, enemies only seem to spawn as you play so you're never clearing out any area, just wasting time without making progress if you're not charging the exit door with kills.

The combat system is bloated already. Why do we need to have 2 items, an ultimate ability, some kind of special weapon and bullet time? Good movement that's actually useful in combat is enough to be interesting and fun, everything else just detracts from it and leads to dev time being devoted to additions to combat instead of the core mechanics.

After the recent update, the game reduces you to a level of weakness that makes the game basically unplayable. Maybe if you can get past the beginning, it's fun changes, but as it stands, this is no longer fun to play.

Short version: The game used to be advertised as a short and sweet experience that you could pick up and play, feeling the rush and frenetic action of a movement shooter without having to invest too much time with it. It was fun, simple and with a lot of movement options; a lot of different loadouts to make your own experience unique and a boatload of guns to shoot and improve at the upgrade machine, turning them into a total fantasy of fun explosions and absurd firerates; without sacrificing challenge down the line because of the Threat system, making it harder the more you played through the run. Unfortunately the game got turned into a roguelite that forces you to grind through perma upgrades, gatekeeping you from higher difficulties and turning the game into a poverty simulator by not giving you any guns unless you're lucky to find a single weapon chest in a bunker if you ever get to find one.

I used to like the game a lot, it was a very straightforward experience and a small little game to play for a few hours and then drop for a while, come back to it from time to time. It respected the time you spent on it and it even got interesting the more you played it since it gets harder and harder the more enemies you killed. That was until the newest update.

Everything around the update, is great, a complete overhaul and improvement over the original movement mechanics and the gun models. THe enemies are better animated and more characteristic, but when it comes to the gameplay loop it fails very hard in my opinion.

As i said, the game used to be very straightforward, you had loadout cards that gave you starter items and weapons and you could play however you liked, and that was what made me play the game most often than not. But now, it has been seriously capped and butchered to the point where you are not able to progress much even on normal difficulties, because the game has permanent upgrade mechanics tied to a currency you get for completing door events.

With this change all the game does is gate you from harder challenges and puts you at your weakest, forcing you to grind for more and more expensive upgrades, even forcing you to spend that currency on REVEALING more upgrades. It's a total turn off and even games like Hades and Dead Cells, other roguelites with permanent progression, do it much much better than this.

Even if the bunker keys are easier to find now, you are forced to be opening every single trunk on every vehicle until you find one, yes i know you can craft them, but why would i need to waste time doing that when i can be playing the damn game. It chokes you by stripping you from any kind of weapon drop unless you find a chest inside a bunker or a slot machine that costs 800 shards. And even then a bunker is NOT guaranteed to have a weapon chest. It's terrible.

For perspective sake, the game used to have a couple chests per level, you could find the guns you liked eventually and the game wasn't shy about it, it wanted YOU to have fun with it and explore the many guns there were in the game, Unfortunately that's over, and now you have to be sucking absolute rod in order to get a simple SMG that will probably not enable you to clear most enemy waves past Threat 5.

For me, the game is not fun anymore, if i want to feel cucked to hell and back by an upgrade system i rather play a proper roguelite. This is not the game i used to like and it became a total chore to sit through unskippable dramatic cutscenes that add nothing to the game, to then repeat a cycle of having to suffer through the first level with only a pistol that runs out of ammo in no time against hordes and hordes of angry grunts, and not even get enough for a measly shield upgrade back home.

TL;DR: This game is fun moment-to-moment, but at this point I don't recommend buying it unless it’s on sale. It currently feels like a gamefeel-focused sandbox that exists for the developer to play around with adding new cool mechanics. It feels iffy as a product. It’s lacking some crucial polish and has lots of things that get in the way of a smooth player experience. The movement is good, the guns are dope, and the enemies are very satisfying to shoot. But there's no real long-term enjoyment to be had yet, and it can be very frustrating.

Some frustration points:

1) If your run ends you return to the starting hub- but it doesn’t reset for a new run, and it doesn’t let you pick a new starting loadout. Any weapon vendors you've purchased from are still empty, and because you've died you no longer have any money to buy anything else. You're able to start up a new level from here, but it won’t be a fresh run. The only way to do that is to reload the main menu.

2) Money is everything in this game. You kill enemies to get money, and spend that money on in-game items. However, when you lose a life mid run, you lose ALL of your money. If this happens to you before you've earned any high-level weapons or gear, you may as well restart your run. The challenge level stays the same, but you have to grind to get your progress back. This is a huge pacing killer.

3) Enemy spawning can be really jank. They frequently spawn directly on top of other enemies, even ones that have already died. This creates a 'hydra' effect where you kill an enemy and it is immediately replaced, sometimes multiple times in a row. Enemies also frequently spawn inside of walls, or even on top of you.

4) Quite a few times I've gone so fast that I get stuck in walls, particularly around doorways/entrances to bunkers. Sometimes you can escape, sometimes you get softlocked and have to restart.

5) By default there are multiple keybinds applied to the same keys. I don't know why this is the case, there are absolutely enough keys not being used. You can fix this with rebinds EXCEPT for melee/interact, which are stuck on the same key. Also, you can swap weapons with the number keys, which is good, but you cannot rebind them; you CAN, however, bind additional functions on those keys. Its messy.

6) Navigation is confusing at first. The hub where you start every run is practically empty. The shop— the main reason for the hub to exist in the first place— is out of the way and took me some time to find on my first playthough. The levels themselves can be confusing too, and the 'orange door' icon that appears in the tutorial to show you where to go is missing during normal gameplay. I eventually learned the landmarks, but since everything is all flat-shaded with neon wireframes, its easy to get turned around.

7) Every run starts with a platforming sequence that is supposed to demonstrate a contextual movement mechanic- monkey bars, ladders, etc. Theres even a little video tab that shows you how to interact with them. However on your first run there is no explanation of the general movement mechanics. You can wander around the hub and experiment before you enter the level, but there's no way to know all the moves unless you look in the controls options. So in my first run, when I was faced with a Dash Point tutorial, I got stuck for about 10 minutes.

Here's what was going on: Normally, you can only dash horizontally- and dashing refreshes your double jump, but not anything else (the game doesn't tell you this). I was confusing this refresh for the effect of hitting the dash point (there is no feedback when you hit it), and so spent tens of tries assuming It just required really tight timing or something. It really works like this: If you are close enough to the dash point, haven't yet used your double jump, and look directly at it, it flashes green. If you dash when its green, you can dash vertically AND your dash is lengthened to reach the dash point. THEN you get both your dash and double jump back. If I that tutorial popup hadn't disappeared after about 8 seconds, I might've figured this out faster. But on my own, it took me about 10 minutes. And after all that, I don't think I saw a single dash point in the following level.

8) There is only one boss and it is an absolute pushover. The first two times I fought it I took no damage at all. Killing it gives you nothing- no money, no gun, nada- and loops you back to the hub. The level leading up to it is full of vendors, including a loop pedestal that normally allows you to replay the level once its completed. However, this doesn't work on the boss stage- and even if it did, you get no money, so what’s the point of revisiting the vendors?

9) There’s an optional combat arena you can enter if you complete all combat stone challenges in a level. Completing the arena gives you a BFG equivalent, which is nice- but if you enter it again later in the run, you just get the same reward again with no added benefit. Also I've gotten softlocked here because the enemies didn’t spawn in, and there's no way to leave unless you kill them all.

10) The combat stones are boring and frustrating. Using them summons a number of Seeker nests, and you have to kill them all as they continually spawn Seekers- the most annoying enemy in the game. They float around, then glow orange and divebomb you instantly. Its basically impossible to dodge, so you have to kill them first. They do insane damage and can gang up on you easily, especially if you're already fighting a wave of enemies. You cannot outrun them- the divebomb seems to have perfect accuracy and infinite range, and they will follow you across the entire map. And the spawners are bullet sponges, so you have to hard focus them. If you have a really powerful weapon you can burn them down quickly- so its a challenge that is only recommended to do once you have the gear to handle it, at which point it becomes dull. So it's either a pain in the ass, or an obvious uninteresting choice. Just make sure you don't have to reload while you're bursting down the spawners and you're fine.

11) The reload animations, while quite satisfying, are generally pretty long. Most weapons can dump entire mags quickly, so you often spend more time reloading than you do shooting. Furthermore there is no short reload if you still have bullets in the magazine, so you may as well always expend your entire mag mid combat. Swapping weapons interrupts reloads as well, and you cannot change fire modes while reloading. You can use equipment while reloading, which enables some strategy, but I wish there was more you could do to alleviate the scurge of constantly reloading- especially when you get multiple weapon slots, and ESPECIALLY since weapons of the same type share an ammo pool. It just slows the game down.

12) There is a bullet time mechanic, which I keep forgetting exists. Sometimes I feel like its there because the game can move so quickly it can be difficult to contol, especially during combat. Its probably vital to use once you get used to it, but the mechanic is never explained or tutorialized, so I only realized it was there when I was looking at the keybindings.

13) Lastly, as of time of writing, there appears to be no conclusion to a run other than death. Its fine to have a game that lets you loop and get stronger for as long as possible, but there should at least be a way to purposefully end a run. Otherwise eventually it just gets boring.

Short Version: Weird and annoying mechanics make the game a confusing on the best things to do during a level, like exploring and taking your time, or playing quickly using your crazy movement abilities. Levels are very samey and difficult to navigate due to being monotonous. Starting a new run after death is annoying due to two cutscenes and a separate little map you must go through before returning to the hub. It's strange over-all.

Long version: The health system is much better. You don't have to kill enemies right next to you or be forced to use the medkit equipment: you can gain health by using bandage equipment, picking up healthkits around the level, or pick up enemy health bits they drop. You can also find secrets and, for some reason randomly sometimes, get an overshield that makes you quite a bit tankier.

It still takes forever to get the points to buy items, use machines, etc. Keys, which function differently than how they did in the previous milestone, makethis annoying, as they are now a new currency of sorts. You get keys (rarely) from enemies and interactables or guaranteed from hanging red lights. They are used to open "bunkers," little sealed off areas with weapon upgrade benches, places to buy items/weapons, and multiple interactables, depending on your luck. The best way to get anything is to find a bunker, but for that you need a key, and the fastest way is to explore the level, which is quite risky if you do so too fast.

As you explore the level, it triggers enemy pods to spawn. Enemies no longer constantly trickle in around you like the previous milestone, they only seem to spawn for a little bit after a pod activates. If you got through the level and activate all the pods to explore and find keys quickly, you become swarmed by enemies and die quite quickly, too. If you take it slow and try to kill every enemy to get points/try for keys, that increases the enemy threat level quickly, making more enemies spawn per pod and lets more difficult enemy types spawn.
If you manage to activate all nearby pods and defeat them, you are left with an empty section of the level and are forced to progress to get anything of note by finding more pods. If you found a bunker but don't have a key, but get one later, you have to backtrack through a now empty part of the level with no enemies to fight. If you activated the last pod in a level, the only way to fight more enemies is to trigger the door-unlocking event...

The most annoying part is that, to unlock the door to beat a level, you are forced to kill a set amount of enemies, an annoying element from the previous milestone that carried over. This forces you to raise the enemy level, making the door-unlocking fight even more swamped with enemies and making it possible for new enemy types to spawn as you kill the amount needed. Unlike teleporter events from Risk of Rain, which are usually quite fast and end upon killing a boss rather than a massive swarm of enemies, these can last quite a bit if you've had rotten luck and were unable to get any weapons or equipment during the level. Unlike Risk of Rain where enemies get harder as time progresses in the run and constantly spawn near you and trickle in, in this it seems to be a bizarre system where you're punished in terms of difficulty for going fast and also punished if you are meticulous and go slow. Each enemy gives a measly amount of points, and as the level increases those points become much more dangerous to get for the same amount per enemy.

There are new enemy types and all enemies have been redesigned. In most cases, their inspiration is obvious, which leads to enemies like Imps standing out noticeably from the rest, where most are inspired by the Covenant from Halo. Enemies can now teleport short distance and climb around, making them annoyingly mobile and relentless, capable of stalking you for a good while and fire pot-shots at you from extreme distances if they can't get to you due to water or pits. At least they all use projectiles. Weapons have had a complete visual replacement. Where before they had their inspirations, like the Heavy Rifle being the Covenant Carbine (except ballistic), most newer designs are more generic. Weapons are more "modern" and feature tac-rails and the like rather than being simplistic and more imaginative. A lot also appear completely dark rather than being colorful with tron-style glowing parts, which seems odd to me.

The levels are still aimless blobs of various parts that lack significant landmarks besides the rare open clearing or orange bunker doors. It is very difficult to get your bearings in a level otherwise, as everything tends to be a monotonous black with occasional highlights besides the wall-run green/white billboard-things.

If you die during a run, you have to watch a prolonged dieing cutscene, end up in a permanent upgrade shrine area, use the shrine, even if you can't buy anything, have a loading screen, and then end back in the hub map after another cutscene. You can't skip either cutscene (as far as I know), so you have to go through all these steps before you can start another run every single time. I'm confused as to why you enter the small shrine map between the cutscenes when the hub also has a shrine that offers the same permanent upgrades to buy.

I really don't get the purpose of how the mechanics work and function together. Similar to ADACA, there are a whole bunch of ideas crammed into one package that makes the whole thing a bit muddled. 
Should I play fast like the movement wants me to, or slow so I can get points to actually get things? 
Should I be backtracking so much for bunkers or just move on to the next level with no real gain? 
Is it better to kill enemy pods for maximum points or leave stragglers so you don't raise the enemy level too quickly?
I am just left confused on what the best and intended way to play actually is, and the game doesn't offer help in that regard.
